ghs.assessment: The repeated はい is a rapid string of acknowledgments such as "yes" or "okay." "Quick" turns it into a command about speed.

highlights.text: great-great-granddaughter gyaru in a group going to (pre)school.

rows.jp: きっと『イルクーツク・マニア』と同じくらい世界的にも使用回数の少ない単語に違いない。
rows.en: It had to rank somewhere around “Irkutsk mania” among the least-used phrases on earth.

ghs.en: No mistaking this, it's a word that is certain to attain the same level of worldwide popularity and frequency of utilization as Irkutsk Mania.
ghs.assessment: The joke says the word must be used as rarely worldwide as 'Irkutsk Mania.' The English omits the low-frequency judgment and can imply comparable popularity instead.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It must be used about as rarely worldwide as “Irkutsk Mania.”'

highlights.text: No mistaking this, it's a word that is certain to attain the same level of worldwide popularity and frequency of utilization as Irkutsk Mania.

rows.jp: 「そのピティワードに免じて見逃してやりたいところだが、どこの星から来たのかくらい白状していけ！」
rows.en: “That little mercysyllable almost earns you a pass, but first confess which planet you came from!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you do desire me to deferentially overlook that pitiful affectation of a word, then confess at least from which star you come from!"
ghs.assessment: ピティワード continues the 'pretty word' joke, not a pitiful affectation. The source says he would like to let her off in consideration of it but demands a confession; the English turns that into a condition about what she desires and also duplicates 'from.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'd like to let you off for that pretty word, but at least confess what planet you're from!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If you do desire me to deferentially overlook that pitiful affectation of a word, then confess at least from which star you come from!"

ghs.en: Nanaka: "I! Told! You! Ea-ar-th-ling I am!"

rows.jp: 「うそだ、地球人の気配と違う！」
rows.en: “Liar! Your presence feels nothing like an Earthling’s!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You lie, you have a different presence than an earthling!"

rows.jp: 俺は得意のカラデの構えを取った。
rows.en: I assumed the stance of my signature karade.

ghs.en: I took a most skillful Karade stance.

rows.jp: カラデは究極の格闘技だ。
rows.en: Karade is the ultimate martial art.

ghs.en: Karade is the ultimate martial art.

rows.jp: 白い指先が俺をびっと指す。
rows.en: One white finger snapped out toward me.

ghs.en: A white fingertip shot out, pointed at me.

rows.jp: 振り返って、視界が学校をとらえて数秒。
rows.en: I turned. The school filled my vision. Several seconds passed.

ghs.en: Turning around, my field of vision was captured by the school for several moments.
ghs.assessment: The metaphor and aspect are clumsy, but the line does not fully reverse the source.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the source image and aspect naturally.

highlights.text: Turning around, my field of vision was captured by the school for several moments.

ghs.assessment: The English changes number and deictic reference while retaining the local referent.
ghs.remedy: Match the source number and deixis.

highlights.text: No answers there.

rows.jp: 彼女はいなくなっていた。
早いで済まされる現象ではないのだが。

ghs.en: Not a Phenomenon that's going to be settled quickly.
ghs.assessment: The source says this phenomenon cannot be explained away merely by saying she was fast. 'Not ... settled quickly' instead describes the speed at which the phenomenon will be resolved.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This wasn't something that could be explained away by saying she was fast.'

highlights.text: Not a Phenomenon that's going to be settled quickly.

ghs.assessment: ぉゃ is a tiny puzzled 'oh?' or 'huh?' 'Mother of...?' invents an unfinished oath unrelated to the utterance.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Oh?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "......mother of...?"

rows.jp: 蝉も鳴いてない、静かな新学期だった。
rows.en: Not even the cicadas were singing. It was a quiet first day of term.

ghs.en: It was a quiet new school term, when even the cicadas didn't cry.
